name: Solenne Atelier Bias-Cut Blouse
description:
A fluid, long-sleeved blouse cut on the bias in a silk-protein weave that moves like water and catches light along every seam. The collar is a loose, draped cowl that can be worn forward or folded back, and the sleeves taper to a soft cuff that buttons with a single mother-of-nacre synthetic. The color is 'pale mercury' — a shifting silver-white that reads differently depending on the light source, cool in natural light, almost warm under incandescent. The drape is architectural: it falls perfectly, which is the result of the bias cut combined with the weight of the fabric.

Solenne Atelier is a small Tier 5 house operating out of the upper Spire district, designing for clients who have already stopped looking at price tags. The blouse is made to measure, delivered in tissue and a cedar-lined box, and comes with a card noting the name of the person who sewed it. It is, in every technical sense, just a blouse. But it is the best blouse.
what_it_says: You are at the top. You dress without effort because the effort was done for you, invisibly, by someone whose name you actually know.
worn_by: people attending events where clothing is assessed at a glance and judged correctly
story_hooks: The artisan whose name is on the card inside a particular blouse has gone missing — and the last client who received one with her name is being asked questions.
Solenne Atelier keeps meticulous records of every client — a ledger that would be extraordinarily valuable to anyone wanting to map Spire social networks.
A Tier 2 woman finds a Solenne blouse in a donation bin, unworn, tags still on. The cedar box is missing. She wears it to a job interview and something changes.
